chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to pray from the night thirteen rak'at, including the Witr, and the two rak'at of Fajr, during travel and residence.
ai.seo_question: How many rak'at did the Prophet Muhammad pray during the night according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) regarding the total number of night prayers, explicitly including the two voluntary rak'at of Fajr within the count of thirteen. This narration is central to the Shia scholarly debate on whether the Fajr sunnah is part of the Qiyam al-Layl or a separate entity, with many jurists citing it to support the practice of praying them as a unit or closely linked sequence. It underscores the Prophet's consistent devotion, maintaining this specific count regardless of whether he was traveling or residing in Medina.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allahsaww used to pray, from the night (Salāts), thirteen Rak’at, from it being Al-Witr, and two Rak’at of Al-Fajr, during the travel and the staying’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said
that the Messenger of Allah would perform thirteen Rak‘at at night of which one Rak‘at was al-Witr and two Rak‘at of the morning whether on a journey or at home.’”
